assessment: This valuable work suggests a novel mechanism of purifying selection by which programmed cell death contributes to the selective removal of mtDNA deletion mutations in C. elegans. The authors demonstrate with convincing evidence that mtDNA deletion is more abundant in the offspring of older mothers and that activators for programmed cell death are required to suppress the accumulation of defective mtDNA in the germline of C. elegans. Because of the likely central role of mtDNA deletions in aging and age-dependent diseases, this work will be of interest to scientists in the field of mitochondrial biology as well as aging.
